schema: §2.7 (v0.50) -- complete per-sentence segment disposition, superseding §21 R6's not_annotatable-only shape. `not_annotatable` (R6's original array, the only key run_scoring.load_not_annotatable() reads) is preserved for scoring and holds every NOT_OBLIGATION_BEARING / NOT_ANNOTATABLE / EXCLUDED span. `dispositions` is the full per-sentence record §2.7 requires, covering ANNOTATED and AMBIGUOUS spans too, which `not_annotatable` deliberately excludes -- an AMBIGUOUS span is an open reviewer question, not a settled non-item, and including it in the scoring array would resolve it silently.

dispositions.span_text: Bellicum will reimburse Miltenyi for Third Party royalties and/or license fees, if any, owed by Miltenyi under Third Party license agreements existing as of the Effective Date as set forth on Exhibit D solely to the extent Miltenyi's exercise of rights under such licenses is required 27 Miltenyi Biotec-Bellicum Supply Agreement (Execution Copy, March 27, 2019) to supply Miltenyi Product to Bellicum under this Agreement for the Permitted Use; and further provided that amounts owed under such Third Party license agreements have not otherwise been passed through to Bellicum and are actually paid by Miltenyi to Miltenyi's licensor(s).

Bellicum acknowledges that the potential volume of such Third Party royalties and/or license fees under applicable Third Party license agreements will be as set forth on Exhibit D, as updated from time to time by Miltenyi.
dispositions.reason: ‘Bellicum acknowledges that ... will be as set forth on Exhibit D’ states a future FACT about what an exhibit will say, not a party's undertaking -- §3.2's own 'will'-ambiguity rule: 'will' is not an obligation at all when it states a future fact about the agreement ('this Agreement will terminate on...'); this is the identical shape one level removed via an acknowledgment. Matches §2.7's own text naming 'an acknowledgment' as a no-modal-verb class alongside a rights-reservation and a copular status clause.

dispositions.span_text: If, during the Term of this Agreement, the Parties mutually agree to obtain additional Third Party licenses to enable the Permitted Use of Miltenyi Products by Bellicum, its Affiliates, Subcontractors, and/or Licensees under this Agreement, and such additional licenses give rise to Third Party royalties and/or license fees with respect to Bellicum's use of Miltenyi Products under this Agreement, then the Parties will negotiate in good faith which Party(ies) is/are responsible for payment of such Third Party royalties and/or license fees.
Miltenyi, acting reasonably, reserves the right to defer the inclusion of additional Miltenyi Products in Exhibit B hereto until the Parties have reached agreement on this matter.
dispositions.reason: This is surplus clause #1 in the investigation's table -- 'Miltenyi ... reserves the right to defer ... until the Parties have reached agreement'; escalated rather than resolved because Decision 3 (whether §2.5/§2.5.1's clarification is retroactive over this pre-§2.5 segment) is explicitly open, not ruled.

Under the CURRENT §2.5/§2.5.1 test, the clause clears on three independent stakes: a reviewable standard ('acting reasonably' -- §2.5.1's own named discriminator), a bounded observable end-point ('until the Parties have reached agreement'), and a narrow specific object -- distinguished from C04-026 and from §2.5.1's C14-044 negative example. CORROBORATED 2026-09-05, near-verbatim: the cold annotator reached this reading independently and CONFIDENT, listing the IDENTICAL THREE STAKES IN THE SAME ORDER ('acting reasonably' as section 2.5.1's own counter-example to 'sole business judgment'; the bounded observable end-point 'until the Parties have reached agreement'; the narrow specific object against C04-026's ten-verb catch-all) and independently distinguishing section 2.5.1's C14-044 negative example on the same ground. Cold additionally reaches a field this reading does not: temporal RELATIVE_TO_TRIGGER(before, 'the Parties have reached agreement on this matter') with known_gaps ['relative_trigger_preposition'], per section 8.9's v0.34 correction that 'until' was never counted but IS covered by the rule as written -- and section 8.9's own cassette observation records 'until <trigger>' occurring in C04-117 twice, which is this sentence. NARROWED SCOPE: the SUBSTANTIVE question is settled concordantly; what remains is DECISION 3 ALONE -- retroactivity over a segment locked at v0.28 (C04-01 stamps v0.28; section 2.5 is v0.39, section 2.5.1 is v0.41). One Decision 3 ruling disposes of both this span and C11-094 #3. CAVEAT per section 7.1: concordance is a LOWER BOUND on error, not proof.
